subject: english-literature
title: Story versus Discourse
welcome_lead: Russian formalists separated fabula from sjuzhet — events from how they are told. Master the central narratological pair.
meta_desc: Story versus discourse, fabula and sjuzhet at A-Level English Literature.
final_note: You have separated what happens from how it is told — narratology's central distinction.

concepts.def: Russian Formalist term — the chronological events as they 'really' happened in the story-world.
The arrangement and presentation of those events as the reader encounters them (also called plot).
Genette's parallel pair (histoire / récit) — events told versus telling.
Wayne Booth's term — the textual personality the reader infers, distinct from the historical author.
Wolfgang Iser — the reader role inscribed in the text, the receiver the text seems to imagine.
Genette distinguishes extradiegetic (outside the story), diegetic (within), metadiegetic (a story-within-a-story).

walkthroughs.body_html:
Sjuzhet may begin with the ending, flash back, leap forward. Fabula is the chronological skeleton the reader reconstructs.

Detective fiction is the genre that most reveals the gap — the sjuzhet conceals the fabula until the final revelation.
Booth's implied author is the moral personality the reader infers behind the choices of the text. It may differ from the historical author and from any single narrator.
Genette's level distinction tracks frame narratives. In Frankenstein, Walton (extradiegetic), Frankenstein (diegetic) and the creature (metadiegetic) speak from nested levels.

mcqs.q: Why must students distinguish the narrator from the author?
options: It is a religious text used in Catholic services.
The narrator is a constructed voice within the text; the author is the real person who created it. Conflating them misreads irony, unreliable narration and persona.
The narrator and author are different words for the same thing.
The narrator's views are always the author's views.

mcqs.q: What is the structural framework of The Canterbury Tales?
options: It is a religious text used in Catholic services.
A frame narrative — pilgrims travelling to Canterbury tell stories along the way, allowing Chaucer to juxtapose different voices, genres and social classes.
It means it is wrong to write fiction.
It is one continuous story told by Chaucer from beginning to end.
It means authors can never make mistakes when writing.
It means it is wrong to write fiction.
The claim that judging a text by what the author 'intended' is fallacious — the text's meaning lies in the work itself, not the author's stated or guessed intentions.
The narrator and author are different words for the same thing.
